channel.title: Gumshoe News Radio (Harry)
channel.description: Private AM-radio-style news bulletins for Londonderry, NH.
channel.itunes:author: Gumshoe

item.title: Oct 14 PM - 1. Londonderry Weather
item.description: Good evening, and welcome to Gumshoe News Radio for Wednesday, October fourteenth. I'm your anchor. Let's start with your Londonderry weather, from the National Weather Service. For the rest of this afternoon, mostly sunny with a high near seventy-one and a northwest wind around ten miles an hour. Tonight, partly cloudy, with a low around forty-five. Thursday turns cooler: sunny, with a high near fifty-nine. Friday brings rain, a hundred percent chance, with a high near sixty-one, and showers likely Friday night. Saturday clears out but it's chilly, mostly sunny with a high near forty-seven, and Saturday night drops to around twenty-eight, so bring in the plants. Sunday, sunny and fifty-three. Monday, sunny and sixty-two. And Tuesday, mostly sunny with a high near sixty-four.

item.title: Oct 14 PM - 2. US Headlines
item.description: Now the top stories here at home. Inflation picked up in September. Consumer prices rose at a three point seven percent annual rate, driven largely by costlier gasoline, according to the government's report today, as covered by the Wall Street Journal and Reuters. On the campaign trail, the Associated Press reports Republicans are pulling back spending in a handful of front-line House districts, shifting the battle lines three weeks before the November midterms. Next door in Maine, Senator Susan Collins debated her Democratic challenger, Troy Jackson. Kimberly Guilfoyle has resigned as U.S. ambassador to Greece, days after the Wall Street Journal reported she asked a Republican donor to pay off a hundred-thousand-dollar credit card bill. In Florida, the governor says six deaths are now confirmed from Hurricane Isaias, according to Reuters. And in Pennsylvania, a sixth person has died of measles as cases there top eleven hundred. The C D C says it's sending additional support to investigate.

item.title: Oct 14 PM - 3. World Headlines
item.description: Around the world. In Serbia, hundreds rallied outside the independent news site Nova dot R S in Belgrade, after new owners told journalists to accept editors from pro-government outlets or leave. Nearly all the staff chose to stay. Parliamentary elections are October twenty-fifth. In Pakistan, the media regulator has ordered TV channels to stop live coverage of explosions and terror attacks, and to air only government-verified information. It follows emergency rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. In India, young protesters have taken to the streets of New Delhi over a nationwide review of voter rolls that critics say removed millions of names. The Election Commission calls it a routine cleanup. And the Wall Street Journal reports Ukraine says new limits on Starlink are disrupting its military operations.

item.title: Oct 14 PM - 4. Market Wrap
item.description: Time for the market wrap. A rough day on Wall Street after that hot inflation report stirred worries about more interest rate hikes from the Federal Reserve. According to preliminary figures reported by Reuters, the S and P five hundred fell about eighty-four points, or one point one percent, to seven thousand seven hundred twenty-one. The Nasdaq dropped five hundred three points, or nearly one point nine percent, to twenty-six thousand seven hundred one, with A I names like Oracle and CoreWeave hit hardest. The Dow held up best, slipping just forty-five points, less than a tenth of a percent, to fifty-one thousand six hundred twenty-five. Bank stocks also weighed after quarterly results.

item.title: Oct 14 PM - 5. Feel-Good Story
item.description: And now, something to smile about, from the Good News Network. Twenty-one-year-old Brooklyn Green was heading to the movies when she noticed Mary, a woman who has worked in movie theaters for more than forty-five years, pushing a trash cart. Brooklyn posted a short video and started a fundraiser, hoping for maybe a month's rent. Strangers gave more than a hundred thousand dollars on the first day, and by the next morning the total reached a hundred forty-six thousand. Now Mary gets to find out what rest feels like.

item.title: Oct 14 PM - 6. Local & Civic Dates
item.description: Finally, a civic reminder for Londonderry. The general election is Tuesday, November third. To register before Election Day, the Secretary of State says registration closes six to thirteen days before the election, depending on your town, so check with the Londonderry Town Clerk at Town Hall, open weekdays eight thirty to five. And New Hampshire also lets you register at your polling place on Election Day. That's your news for now. Stay tuned to Gumshoe News Radio, and just message me if you'd like more on any story.
